docRequirement: agent-sdk/mcp.md:891 — "The SDK applies the same MCP output limit as Claude Code. When a tool result is larger than 25,000 tokens, the full output is saved to a file and the tool result is replaced with an error message that names the file path, so the agent can read the output back in portions. Raise the limit with the MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS environment variable." The linked page it defers to for "the full behavior" fixes the detail: mcp.md:1022 "the default maximum is 25,000 tokens", :1021 the limit is adjusted via `MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS`, :1023 the env var "applies to tools that don't declare their own limit. Tools that set `anthropic/maxResultSizeChars` use that value instead for text content, regardless of what `MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS` is set to", and :1040 that annotation is honoured "up to a hard ceiling of 500,000 characters".
current: The persist-to-disk mechanism itself matches: an MCP result is guarded in `McpClientPool.callTool` (packages/shared/src/mcp/mcp-pool.ts:2170-2178) via `guardLargeResult`, which saves the full text under `<session>/long_responses/` and returns a replacement message naming the absolute path (packages/shared/src/utils/large-response.ts:634-641, :666-671, :700-708). The NUMBER is wrong and the override is absent. (1) The MCP call site passes `maxResultSizeChars` but no `contextWindow` (mcp-pool.ts:2171-2177), so the threshold is `tokenLimitFor(undefined)` = `TOKEN_LIMIT` = 12000 estimated tokens (large-response.ts:42, :141-147, :633). (2) No env override exists anywhere: `grep -ran MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS` over the repo (binary-safe, node_modules/.references/dist excluded) hits only docs JSON, and there is no `NESSY_`-prefixed counterpart; large-response.ts contains no `process.env` read at all. This is not a rename artifact — the fork does port sibling knobs under its own prefix (`NESSY_MCP_TOOL_IDLE_TIMEOUT` at mcp-pool.ts:1959; the `CLAUDE_CODE_*` → `NESSY_*` mapping table at packages/shared/src/config/background-task-settings.ts:9-12). (3) Two SECOND guards re-decide the same MCP result at an even lower threshold and without the per-tool annotation: packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts:1829-1835 guards every `tool_result` event with `contextWindow` and no `maxResultSizeChars` — and MCP proxy tools reach it, because the Claude backend serves them from an SDK MCP server whose handler returns `pool.callTool`'s text (claude-agent.ts:616-624) and `createToolResult` has no MCP exclusion (packages/shared/src/agent/backend/base-event-adapter.ts:205-221); packages/shared/src/agent/local-tools/runtime.ts:59 → :338-352 does the same for `executeMcpTool` results (:289-295). `tokenLimitFor` with a context window can only LOWER the limit — `Math.min(TOKEN_LIMIT, 10% of window)`, floor 2000 (large-response.ts:141-147). (4) The per-tool annotation is read and clamped correctly (`anthropic/maxResultSizeChars` at mcp-pool.ts:213 and :1933-1940, ceiling `MAX_DECLARED_RESULT_SIZE_CHARS = 500_000` at large-response.ts:57, clamp at :620-624) but composes as raise-only: `if (declaredAllowance !== undefined && text.length <= declaredAllowance) return null` (:625-628), then the normal check still runs.
divergence: Three deltas, in descending size. (a) THE NUMBER: our MCP persist threshold is 12,000 estimated tokens, the doc's is 25,000 — so every MCP result in the ~12k–25k token band (roughly 48KB–100KB of plain text) is taken off the model and replaced with a file reference where Claude Code hands it over inline. On the Claude backend and on the local-tools path the effective number is lower still, `min(12000, 10% of the model's context window)` with a 2,000-token floor, because the second guard passes `contextWindow`. (b) THE OVERRIDE IS ABSENT, not misnamed: there is no `MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS` and no `NESSY_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS` — nothing reads any env var here, so a user who follows Claude's docs and exports `MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS=50000` gets no effect whatsoever. (c) COMPOSITION OF THE PER-TOOL ANNOTATION: the value and the 500,000-char ceiling are right, only the composition differs — mcp.md:1023/:1054 says a declaring tool uses its value "instead" of the token limit for text content, ours only raises (large-response.ts:625-628), so a server declaring a value BELOW the default is not honoured downward; and because the Claude/local-tools second guard never receives `maxResultSizeChars`, a declared allowance that legitimately kept a 120,000-char result inline in the pool is re-persisted one layer up, defeating the annotation on those backends.

change.what: New reader: `export const MCP_OUTPUT_TOKEN_LIMIT_DEFAULT = 25_000` and `export function mcpOutputTokenLimit(env: EnvRecord = process.env): number` reading `NESSY_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS` — the fork spelling of `MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS`. Copy the parse shape of `mcpAutoBackgroundDelayMs` (packages/shared/src/config/background-task-settings.ts:118-122): trim, empty → default, non-integer or <= 0 → default. Carry the `MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS` → `NESSY_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS` mapping in the doc comment, in the style of background-task-settings.ts:9-12, and cite mcp.md:1021-1023.

Make the threshold injectable instead of bumping the global. Do NOT change `TOKEN_LIMIT = 12000` (:42) — its 15k→12k lowering carries a recorded reason (:36-40) and it governs Read/Bash/api-tools results, which this page does not bind. Instead: (1) `tokenLimitFor(contextWindow: number | undefined, baseLimit: number = TOKEN_LIMIT)` at :141-147, substituting `baseLimit` for `TOKEN_LIMIT` in both branches; (2) add `tokenLimit?: number` to the `guardLargeResult` opts object (:554-575) and use it at :633 as the `baseLimit`, forwarding it into the `handleLargeResponse` call at :634-640; (3) add the same field to `HandleLargeResponseOptions` (:519-527) and use it in that function's own re-check at :659 so the two checks cannot disagree. Optional, for divergence (c): at :620-628 make a defined `declaredAllowance` the SOLE text gate (`return text.length <= declaredAllowance ? null : persist`) instead of an early-return shortcut — note the page contradicts itself here (:1023 "instead", :1040 "raises"), so record whichever reading is taken.

One line: add `tokenLimit: mcpOutputTokenLimit(),` to the options object, next to the existing conditional `maxResultSizeChars`. This is the site the doc sentence is actually about; everything else here already matches.

Stop the second guard from re-deciding MCP results at the local-tool number. When `event.toolName?.startsWith('mcp__')`, pass `tokenLimit: mcpOutputTokenLimit()` and omit `contextWindow` (which can only lower it, large-response.ts:141-147). Without this edit the mcp-pool change is invisible on the Claude backend: the pool lets a 20k-token result through and this guard persists it anyway. Do not blanket-skip `mcp__` names — MCP servers configured straight into the SDK (not pool-routed) are guarded ONLY here, so skipping would remove their guard entirely.

Same treatment for the MCP branch: when `call.operation.kind` is the MCP proxy kind handled by `executeMcpTool` (:275-295), pass `tokenLimit: mcpOutputTokenLimit()` and omit `contextWindow`. This runtime is constructed by both the nestor-cloud tool executor (backend/nestor-cloud/tool-executor.ts:101) and the Pi subprocess (packages/pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:1551), so leaving it out keeps the old 12k/context-scaled number on those backends.

Add one positive/negative pair for the new `tokenLimit` option: a ~20k-token text passes with `tokenLimit: 25_000` and persists with the default. The existing four cases (:84-127) pin the unchanged default path and must stay green untouched.

blastRadius: `guardLargeResult` has 12 call sites across packages/shared/src/sources/api-tools.ts:284, packages/shared/src/agent/local-tools/runtime.ts:348, packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts:1829, packages/shared/src/mcp/mcp-pool.ts:2171 and packages/pi-agent-server/src/local-tools/tool-wrapper.ts:69 — keeping the new option optional and leaving `TOKEN_LIMIT` at 12000 is what stops this from becoming a change to Read/Bash/HTTP result handling. `tokenLimitFor` and `TOKEN_LIMIT` are also read by `handleLargeResponse` (:659), so the new field must be threaded there or the two checks disagree. Tests that touch this surface: packages/shared/src/utils/__tests__/large-response.test.ts, packages/shared/src/utils/__tests__/binary-detection.test.ts, packages/shared/src/mcp/__tests__/proxy-tool-names.test.ts, packages/shared/src/mcp/__tests__/mcp-pool-descriptor-cache.test.ts. No wire or schema boundary is crossed: no IPC envelope, no persisted record shape, no core/message.ts event changes — the new option is in-process only. It DOES change a filesystem side effect (which results land in `<session>/long_responses/`), which is user-visible in existing sessions and in the CDP live cases, and it adds a new user-facing env knob, so docs need a row (precedent: docs/architecture/fork-subagents.md:32 documents the `NESSY_FORK_SUBAGENT` mapping) and the parity audit row for this page needs updating. One environment check: the local-tools runtime also runs inside the Pi subprocess (packages/pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:1551), so confirm `NESSY_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS` is inherited into that spawn the way `NESSY_MCP_AUTO_BACKGROUND_MS` is.
userImpact: Concrete and reachable today. Call any MCP tool that returns a mid-sized text payload — a GitHub issue list, a DB schema dump, a Confluence/Jira page fetch, a `tools/list`-style inventory — sized roughly 48KB–100KB. In Claude Code the agent receives it inline; in Nessy the chat shows the tool returning a `[Response too large]`-style replacement naming a `long_responses/…txt` path plus an LLM summary, and the agent has to spend an extra turn Reading the file back, with whatever the summary dropped simply gone from the turn. On the Claude backend, or any model with a context window under 120k, it bites earlier still — the second guard scales the limit to 10% of the window (floor 2,000 tokens), so an ~8KB MCP result already spills on a 64k-window model. And the documented escape hatch does not exist: a user who reads Claude's docs and exports `MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS=50000` sees exactly no change, with no warning that the variable is unrecognised. Separately, a server that declared `anthropic/maxResultSizeChars` to keep its big result inline gets that honoured by the pool and then undone one layer up on the Claude and local-tools backends, so the annotation appears not to work.
